exposure: Microorganisms in cervical cultures (Escherichia coli, Group B Streptococcus, Enterobacterales, beta-hemolytic Streptococci)
cohort: Postpartum women suspected of having endometritis.
finding: While cervical cultures can identify potential pathogens in postpartum endometritis, their clinical utility is questionable due to the polymicrobial nature of the disease and the isolation of commensal microorganisms, with no significant differences in disease severity across various microorganism groups.
